name: CockroachDB
tagline: Postgres-wire distributed SQL built to survive node, zone and region failures with serializable transactions.
description: CockroachDB is a distributed SQL database that shards data into Raft-replicated ranges and runs serializable ACID transactions across them, so a cluster keeps accepting reads and writes through node, zone or region loss. It speaks the PostgreSQL wire protocol and much of its dialect, and adds multi-region table locality controls that pin rows to geographies for latency or data residency. It is a strong fit for globally distributed OLTP systems of record such as payments, identity and inventory. Since late 2024 every self-hosted binary ships under the proprietary CockroachDB Software License, free only for individuals and smaller companies, so budget for an enterprise contract at scale.

pricing.notes: Self-hosted Enterprise Free license for individuals and small businesses (annual renewal, telemetry required); CockroachDB Cloud Basic is usage-based with a free monthly allowance; Standard/Advanced are provisioned.

scale.notes: Automatic range splitting and rebalancing; REGIONAL BY ROW and GLOBAL tables control write latency vs. read locality across regions.

strengths: Serializable isolation by default across shards, with no application-level sharding
Survives zone or region loss without manual failover thanks to Raft replication
Row-level geo-partitioning (REGIONAL BY ROW) for data residency and local-latency writes
PostgreSQL wire compatibility lets most Postgres drivers and ORMs connect unchanged
Online schema changes and rolling upgrades without downtime
Changefeeds stream row changes to Kafka, cloud storage or webhooks
weaknesses: Self-hosted use now requires a proprietary license; larger companies must pay
Single-row write latency is higher than a single-node Postgres because of consensus
Not a drop-in Postgres: many extensions (PostGIS internals, pg_cron, etc.) are unavailable
Serializable retries (40001 errors) must be handled in application code
Analytical queries over large scans are slow compared with columnar engines
useCases: Global payments and ledger systems of record
Identity, account and session metadata across regions
Inventory and order management with strict consistency
Data-residency workloads that must pin rows to a country
Replacing hand-sharded Postgres or MySQL fleets
notIdealFor: Workloads relying on niche Postgres extensions
Tiny apps where a single Postgres instance suffices
Teams that need a permissive open-source license
